questions.explanation: Life experience up to now, with no finished time: present perfect. Adverbs like 'never' go between 'have' and the participle.

multipleChoice.prompt: I ___ to London, but I'd love to go.

gapFill.prompt: I ___ (never / be) to London, but I'd love to go.

errorCorrection.sentence: I never have been to London.
accepted: I have never been to London.

transformation.original: This is my first time in London.

questions.explanation: Something that started in the past and is still true: present perfect + for (a duration) or since (a starting point).

multipleChoice.prompt: I ___ at Google for three years.

gapFill.prompt: I ___ (work) at Google since 2022.

errorCorrection.sentence: I work at Google since 2022.
accepted: I have worked at Google since 2022.
I have been working at Google since 2022.

transformation.original: I started working at Google three years ago.
accepted: have been working at Google for

questions.explanation: Past perfect (had + participle) shows which of two past actions happened first.

multipleChoice.prompt: When I arrived at the station, the train ___.

gapFill.prompt: When I arrived at the station, the train ___ (already / leave).

errorCorrection.sentence: When I arrived, the meeting has already started.
accepted: When I arrived, the meeting had already started.

transformation.original: The train left and then I arrived at the station.
transformation.before: When I arrived at the station, the train

questions.explanation: Future perfect continuous (will have been + -ing) describes how long an action will have lasted by a point in the future.

multipleChoice.prompt: By next year, I ___ English with Tay for three years.

gapFill.prompt: By next year, I ___ (study) English with Tay for three years.

errorCorrection.sentence: By next year, I will be studying English for three years.
accepted: By next year, I will have been studying English for three years.

transformation.original: I started studying English with Tay two years ago, and I'll continue next year.
transformation.after: English with Tay for three years.

questions.explanation: Almost certain about the past: must have + participle. Almost certain it's impossible: can't have + participle.

multipleChoice.prompt: The streets are wet. It ___ last night.

gapFill.prompt: The streets are wet. It ___ (must / rain) last night.

errorCorrection.sentence: The streets are wet. It must rained last night.
accepted: The streets are wet. It must have rained last night.

transformation.original: I'm sure it rained last night.

questions.explanation: To say something is impossible in the present, use can't be, not mustn't be.

multipleChoice.prompt: He ___ hungry. He had a huge lunch an hour ago.

gapFill.prompt: He ___ hungry. He had a huge lunch an hour ago.

errorCorrection.sentence: He mustn't be hungry. He had a huge lunch an hour ago.
accepted: He can't be hungry. He had a huge lunch an hour ago.
He couldn't be hungry. He had a huge lunch an hour ago.

transformation.original: I'm sure he isn't hungry; he just had lunch.

questions.explanation: Two modals can't go together (would can). Use a modal + 'be able to' instead.

multipleChoice.prompt: If I really liked the city, maybe I ___ live there.

gapFill.prompt: If I really liked the city, maybe I would ___ (able) live there.

errorCorrection.sentence: Maybe I would can live there.
accepted: Maybe I would be able to live there.

transformation.original: Maybe living there would be possible for me.

questions.explanation: Would like is followed by 'to' + verb. Modals like can, must, should take the verb with no 'to'.

multipleChoice.prompt: First, I would like ___ the city.

gapFill.prompt: I would like ___ (visit) London someday.

errorCorrection.sentence: I would like visit London someday.
accepted: I would like to visit London someday.
I'd like to visit London someday.

transformation.original: I want to visit London someday.

questions.explanation: Start, begin and continue can take -ing or to + verb, but never the bare verb.

multipleChoice.prompt: I think the best approach is to start ___ Coke Zero.

gapFill.prompt: I think the best approach is to start ___ (drink) Coke Zero.

errorCorrection.sentence: The best approach is start drink Coke Zero.
accepted: The best approach is to start drinking Coke Zero.
The best approach is to start to drink Coke Zero.
The best approach is starting to drink Coke Zero.
The best approach is starting drinking Coke Zero.

transformation.original: You should drink less soda.

questions.explanation: Avoid, enjoy, mind, finish and suggest are followed by -ing. Decide, hope, plan and want are followed by to + verb.

multipleChoice.prompt: We decided ___ by train.

gapFill.prompt: I usually avoid ___ (work) late on Fridays.

errorCorrection.sentence: I enjoy to play foot volley on the beach.
accepted: I enjoy playing foot volley on the beach.

transformation.original: I don't like waking up early.

questions.explanation: Fixed pairs: make a decision, make a mistake, do homework, do a favour, take a break, have a shower.

multipleChoice.prompt: We need to ___ a decision before Friday.

gapFill.prompt: Let's ___ a break and get some coffee.

errorCorrection.sentence: Can you make me a favour?
accepted: Can you do me a favour?
Can you do me a favor?

transformation.original: We need to decide before Friday.

questions.explanation: Get + adjective often means 'become': get tired, get married, get better.

multipleChoice.prompt: My wife and I ___ married in 2019.

gapFill.prompt: I always ___ (get) tired after foot volley.

errorCorrection.sentence: I became tired after the game.
accepted: I got tired after the game.
I got tired after the match.

transformation.original: We became husband and wife in 2019.

questions.explanation: Passive: be + past participle. Use it when the action matters more than who did it.

multipleChoice.prompt: The best paper award ___ to me at the conference.

gapFill.prompt: The best paper award ___ (give) to me at the conference.

errorCorrection.sentence: The paper was present at the conference.
accepted: The paper was presented at the conference.

transformation.original: They gave me the best paper award.

questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle.

multipleChoice.prompt: The new feature ___ yet.

gapFill.prompt: The new feature ___ (not / release) yet.

errorCorrection.sentence: The bug has been fix by the team.
accepted: The bug has been fixed by the team.

transformation.original: The team hasn't fixed the bug yet.

questions.explanation: A question needs only one auxiliary. With 'will', you don't add 'do' or 'does'.

multipleChoice.prompt: ___ proficient if they master this list?

gapFill.prompt: Where ___ you go on your last trip?

errorCorrection.sentence: Does that person will be proficient?

transformation.original: I'd like to know where the station is.

questions.explanation: Question tags: positive sentence, negative tag (and the opposite), using the same auxiliary.

multipleChoice.prompt: You've been to Bahia, ___?

gapFill.prompt: She doesn't like coffee, ___?

errorCorrection.sentence: You work at Google, isn't it?
accepted: You work at Google, don't you?

transformation.original: Where does she live?

questions.explanation: Who/that for the subject of the clause. 'Whom' is only for the object (the prince whom she married).

multipleChoice.prompt: I didn't know the prince ___ married the actress.

gapFill.prompt: Taylor, ___ microphone was taken, was shocked.

errorCorrection.sentence: I didn't know the prince whom married the actress.
accepted: I didn't know the prince who married the actress.
I didn't know the prince that married the actress.

transformation.original: Bartolomeu is a bar. It has a tunnel to the church.

questions.explanation: Where for places, when for times, whose for possession.

multipleChoice.prompt: Ilhéus is the city ___ I presented my paper.

gapFill.prompt: 2019 was the year ___ we got married.

errorCorrection.sentence: That's the colleague which laptop was stolen.
accepted: That's the colleague whose laptop was stolen.

transformation.original: I presented my paper in Ilhéus.

questions.explanation: In reported speech, the tense usually moves back: 'I am' → he said he was.

multipleChoice.prompt: "I'm tired." → He said he ___ tired.

gapFill.prompt: "I will call you." → She said she ___ call me.

errorCorrection.sentence: He told that he was tired.
accepted: He said that he was tired.
He told me that he was tired.
He told me he was tired.

transformation.original: "I'm working from home today," my manager said.

questions.explanation: Reported questions use normal word order (subject + verb) and no question mark.

multipleChoice.prompt: She asked me where ___.

gapFill.prompt: "Do you like sushi?" → He asked me ___ I liked sushi.

errorCorrection.sentence: She asked me where did I work.
accepted: She asked me where I worked.

transformation.original: "Are you coming to the party?" she asked me.

questions.explanation: Your (possessive) vs you (pronoun). Before a noun, use the possessive: your boyfriend.

multipleChoice.prompt: ___ boyfriend should spend more time with you.

gapFill.prompt: He should go out with ___ friends and you together.

errorCorrection.sentence: You boyfriend has to go out with you more.
accepted: Your boyfriend has to go out with you more.

transformation.original: That laptop belongs to me.

questions.explanation: Indefinite pronouns: use 'anything/anyone' in questions and negatives, 'something/someone' in positive sentences.

multipleChoice.prompt: I didn't buy ___ on the trip.

gapFill.prompt: Is there ___ I can do to help?

errorCorrection.sentence: I didn't see nobody at the office.
accepted: I didn't see anybody at the office.
I didn't see anyone at the office.
I saw nobody at the office.
I saw no one at the office.

transformation.original: There was nobody at the office.

questions.explanation: No article when you talk about things in general (people, life, money), unlike Portuguese.

multipleChoice.prompt: ___ is not everything.

gapFill.prompt: I love ___ (dogs / the dogs) in general.

errorCorrection.sentence: The life is too short to work all the time.
accepted: Life is too short to work all the time.

transformation.original: In general, I love dogs.

questions.explanation: Use 'a/an' with jobs and with a singular thing mentioned for the first time.

multipleChoice.prompt: I'm ___ software engineer.

gapFill.prompt: She works as ___ engineer at Google.

errorCorrection.sentence: I'm software engineer at Google.
accepted: I'm a software engineer at Google.

transformation.original: My job is engineering.

questions.explanation: Advice, information, news and feedback are uncountable: no 'a' and no plural.

multipleChoice.prompt: Can I give you ___?

gapFill.prompt: I don't have ___ (many / much) tokens left.

errorCorrection.sentence: She gave me a good advice.
accepted: She gave me some good advice.
She gave me a good piece of advice.
She gave me a piece of good advice.

transformation.original: I don't have many tokens left.

questions.explanation: Words ending in -f/-fe often change to -ves in the plural: wife → wives, life → lives, knife → knives.

multipleChoice.prompt: The old men went to church with their ___.

gapFill.prompt: Cats have nine ___ (life).

errorCorrection.sentence: The old men went to the church with their wifes.
accepted: The old men went to the church with their wives.
The old men went to church with their wives.

transformation.original: There isn't much traffic today.

questions.explanation: Order: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, purpose + noun.

multipleChoice.prompt: She bought a ___ table.

gapFill.prompt: We stayed in a ___ (old / small / charming) hotel.

errorCorrection.sentence: He drives a red big car.
accepted: He drives a big red car.

transformation.original: The car is big and it's red.

questions.explanation: Compound adjectives before a noun use a hyphen and a singular noun: a three-year project, a world-famous singer.

multipleChoice.prompt: It was a ___ project.

gapFill.prompt: Google builds ___ (user / friendly) products.

errorCorrection.sentence: We had a two-hours meeting.

transformation.original: The meeting lasted two hours.

questions.explanation: So + adjective (so good). Such + (a) adjective + noun (such a good trip).

multipleChoice.prompt: It was ___ amazing trip!

gapFill.prompt: The food was ___ good that we went back the next day.

errorCorrection.sentence: It was so a good conference.
accepted: It was such a good conference.

transformation.original: The trip was so amazing.

questions.explanation: Extreme (ungradable) adjectives like amazing, exhausted, freezing go with absolutely, not very.

multipleChoice.prompt: After the match I was ___ exhausted.

gapFill.prompt: The water was ___ freezing! (very / absolutely)

errorCorrection.sentence: The view was very amazing.

transformation.original: I was extremely tired after the trip.

questions.explanation: -ed describes how a person feels (bored). -ing describes what causes the feeling (boring).

multipleChoice.prompt: The meeting was so long that I got ___.

gapFill.prompt: The meeting was really ___ (bore).

errorCorrection.sentence: I'm very interesting in AI.

transformation.original: The movie bored me.

questions.explanation: Surprised/surprising, excited/exciting, tired/tiring: the -ing word is the cause.

multipleChoice.prompt: Winning the award was really ___.

gapFill.prompt: I was ___ (surprise) to win the best paper award.

errorCorrection.sentence: The trip was very tired.

transformation.original: The news surprised everyone.

questions.explanation: Short adjectives: -er/-est (cheaper). Long ones: more/most (more expensive). Never both.

multipleChoice.prompt: London is ___ than Ilhéus.

gapFill.prompt: This is the ___ (good) acarajé I've ever had.

errorCorrection.sentence: This hotel is more cheaper than the other one.
accepted: This hotel is cheaper than the other one.

transformation.original: No city is more beautiful than Rio.

questions.explanation: As + adjective + as for equal things; not as ... as for less.

multipleChoice.prompt: My English isn't ___ my Portuguese.

gapFill.prompt: The new office is twice as big ___ the old one.

errorCorrection.sentence: Foot volley is more fun that football.
accepted: Foot volley is more fun than football.

transformation.original: The old phone was cheaper than the new one.

questions.explanation: Adverbs like just, only, really, always usually go before the main verb (and after 'to' is avoided).

multipleChoice.prompt: I would ___ the city first.

gapFill.prompt: I ___ (always / get up) at 6:30.

errorCorrection.sentence: I go always to the gym in the morning.
accepted: I always go to the gym in the morning.

transformation.original: I go to the gym every day without exception.

questions.explanation: Adverbial phrases like 'from now on' or 'in the long run' usually go at the start or end of the sentence.

multipleChoice.prompt: ___, I'll study grammar every day.

gapFill.prompt: Investing is risky, but ___ the long run it pays off.

errorCorrection.sentence: I visit often my parents.

transformation.original: Starting today, I'll study every day.

questions.explanation: At + time, on + day/date, in + month/year/part of the day.

multipleChoice.prompt: The meeting is ___ Monday ___ 10 a.m.

gapFill.prompt: I was born ___ 1995.

errorCorrection.sentence: I'll see you in Monday.

transformation.original: The conference is in May, on the 12th.

questions.explanation: Common verb + preposition pairs: depend on, listen to, wait for, agree with, be good at.

multipleChoice.prompt: It depends ___ the weather.

gapFill.prompt: I agree ___ you.

errorCorrection.sentence: I'm good in programming.

transformation.original: I'm skilled at public speaking.

questions.explanation: Although/even though + clause (subject + verb). Despite/in spite of + noun or -ing. Never 'despite of'.

multipleChoice.prompt: ___ the rain, we went to the beach.

gapFill.prompt: ___ it was raining, we went to the beach. (Although / Despite)

errorCorrection.sentence: Despite of the rain, we went to the beach.
accepted: Despite the rain, we went to the beach.
In spite of the rain, we went to the beach.

transformation.original: It was raining, but we went to the beach.

questions.explanation: Therefore/as a result introduce a consequence. Whereas contrasts two facts in one sentence.

multipleChoice.prompt: The project was late. ___, the client was unhappy.

gapFill.prompt: I love coffee, ___ my wife prefers tea. (whereas / therefore)

errorCorrection.sentence: I prefer coffee, therefore my wife prefers tea.
accepted: I prefer coffee, whereas my wife prefers tea.
I prefer coffee, while my wife prefers tea.

transformation.original: The project was late, so the client was unhappy.
